author: Cody Nespor
title: WVU volleyball falls just short in comeback bid against Kansas State - NewsBreak
text:
By Cody Nespor No media credit provided. ,
2 hours ago
MORGANTOWN, W.Va. — West Virginia volleyball nearly completed an improbable comeback before ultimately falling, 3-2, to Kansas State in the team’s Big 12 home opener in newly-named Hope Coliseum Wednesday night.
The Mountaineers (12-2, 0-2 Big 12) dropped the first two sets of the match, but came back to win the next two before Kansas State (8-3, 1-2) took the fifth set, ending the Wildcats’ two-game losing streak. Kansas State held on to win the match 3-2 (25-21, 25-23, 22-25, 25-27, 20-18).
“We were right there, played some tight sets,” WVU coach Jen Greeny said. “We served a lot tougher in the third and fourth and then unfortunately just couldn’t get it done.”
Watch: WVU volleyball reacts to near comeback vs. Kansas State West Virginia rushed out to a 5-0 lead in the deciding fifth set, but Kansas State regained the momentum to tie the set at 10-10 and eventually take a 13-10 lead. Two kills by Trinity Sheridan and one from Cassidy Tanton set the Mountaineers up at match point, 14-13.
From there, however, a string of unforced errors by West Virginia allowed Kansas State to keep the game going and ultimately win the set, 20-18. WVU had two service errors and an attacking error at the end of the fifth set before the Wildcats won on an Ava LeGrand kill.
“Credit to Kansas State, they did a nice job of digging some balls and putting pressure from the service line,” Greeny said. “We needed just one more little piece to get over the hump.”
Despite losing the first two sets, West Virginia was in the match the entire time. The first set was tied 20-20 before KSU went on to win 25-21. The second set was tied 23-23 with the Wildcats winning the last two points.
“When we went into the locker room, I felt like a lot of us were feeling some frustration,” junior hitter Nina Horning said. “When you’re down 2-0, it’s a tough feeling. A lot of us were just trying to bring energy the other way.”
WVU overcame an early four-point hole to win set three, 25-22, and battled to win set four, 27-25.
Horning led the Mountaineers with 24 kills, followed closely by Tanton with 23. Both had 11 digs. Sheridan finished third with 13 kills and had four blocks. Maddie McGath had nine kills and a team-high six blocks.
Alexis Finnvold led the team with 46 assists while racking up 12 digs. Libero LonDynn Betts led with 18 digs to go with eight assists.
Shaylee Myers led all players with a match-high 34 kills for Kansas State. LeGrand posted 59 assists.
West Virginia will look to recover from back-to-back conference losses when it hosts BYU on Friday night at 6 p.m. in its Coal Rush game.
